tagline: Down the Branch River valley from Wakefield Corner to Maine.
intro: From the hilltop village of Wakefield Corner the byway comes down NH 153 to Sanbornville, at the outlet of Lovell Lake, where the Branch River begins. Road and river run south together to Union. There NH 125 takes over for Milton, a mill town on the Salmon Falls River, which is the Maine line.

Wakefield Corner was a sledge and stage stop between the seacoast and the White Mountains until the railroad came in 1871 and the center of town moved down the hill to Sanbornville. The Corner kept its old buildings, 26 of them on the National Register.

moments.title: Wakefield Corner
moments.text: The Wakefield Inn went up in 1804 beside the main trade route, and around it stands a hilltop village of antique buildings.

moments.title: New Hampshire Farm Museum
moments.text: On Route 125 a farmstead runs in one connected line, from a small barn by the road to a three-story Great Barn 104 feet long, with Joseph Plumer's house of 1782 in between.

moments.title: Milton
moments.text: Jonas Spaulding opened a leatherboard mill here in 1893, and two of his sons went on to be governors of New Hampshire.
